headline_marked: Education Minister warns [[institution heads to face legal action]] for exam cheating
headline: Education Minister warns institution heads to face legal action for exam cheating
summary: Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon says school and college heads will be held responsible if cheating is found, as changes to the Public Examinations Act are moved to parliament.
details: Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has warned that school and college heads will be held legally responsible if cheating is discovered at their institutions.
The minister stated that cheating has evolved into new forms, comparing it to a coronavirus variant, which has led to changes in The Public Examinations (Offences) Act, 1980.
The proposed changes, which have already been passed by the cabinet, are now heading to parliament for final approval.
Minister Milon explained that because SSC candidates are typically around 16, they cannot be directly penalised but may be placed under probation.
In a separate announcement, the minister confirmed that the 2027 SSC examinations will be held in January to ensure they wrap up before Ramadan and Eid-ul-Fitr.
He also noted a sharp drop in the SSC pass rate to below 60 percent in 2025, suggesting that such a sudden fall indicates weaknesses in teaching or the examination system.
Additionally, the minister announced that teachers who have not received retirement benefits since 2022 will begin receiving them from mid-July.
caption:
School and college heads will now face legal action if cheating is found at their institutions.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon has warned that school and college heads will be held legally responsible if cheating is discovered at their institutions.

The minister stated that cheating has evolved into new forms, comparing it to a coronavirus variant, which has led to changes in The Public Examinations (Offences) Act, 1980.

The proposed changes, which have already been passed by the cabinet, are now heading to parliament for final approval.

Minister Milon explained that because SSC candidates are typically around 16, they cannot be directly penalised but may be placed under probation.

In a separate announcement, the minister confirmed that the 2027 SSC examinations will be held in January to ensure they wrap up before Ramadan and Eid-ul-Fitr.

He also noted a sharp drop in the SSC pass rate to below 60 percent in 2025, suggesting that such a sudden fall indicates weaknesses in teaching or the examination system.

Additionally, the minister announced that teachers who have not received retirement benefits since 2022 will begin receiving them from mid-July.

headline_marked: Rain alert: [[Heavy rainfall likely across Bangladesh]] over next 5 days
headline: Rain alert: Heavy rainfall likely across Bangladesh over next 5 days
summary: Thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected in various regions of the country, causing significant disruption in areas like Mirpur.
details: One hour of rain has already caused a day of suffering for residents of Mirpur, where streets were left waterlogged.
The weather forecast indicates that thunderstorms and heavy rainfall are likely to persist across various regions of Bangladesh for the next five days.
Commuters and residents are advised to stay cautious as the heavy rains continue to affect urban drainage and daily travel.
The pattern of heavy rainfall is expected to impact multiple districts, potentially leading to further waterlogging in low-lying areas.
